reason: Skilled PT/OT/ST rehabilitation followed an inpatient hospital stay for CHF, and the eligibility and documentation agents support coverage; the daily-need question is unsettled but no agent opposes coverage.
All agents agree that documented fluctuating blood pressure and heart rate led to repeated medication adjustments, supporting skilled observation and assessment.
Nurse monitoring of blood sugar logs led to repeated insulin dosage changes, which is skilled observation and assessment, and the visit notes document it.
Post-hospital hematuria with bloody drainage and abnormal labs, under a physician order for skilled nursing, supports skilled observation and assessment.

The record does not show the PT services required a therapist rather than supportive personnel, and the appellant concedes the goals were met, so further therapy is not shown to be reasonable and necessary. The plan of care and physician approval are also not shown.

Only the fragility and joint hypermobility findings support skilled PT. Homebound status and the visit records are unsettled, and the other services (such as the stair-lift transfer teaching and aide visits) rest on appellant assertions alone.
The beneficiary developed a fistula and has ostomies needing care reinforcement, which fall within skilled wound care and ostomy teaching, and all agents support coverage.
The facts contain only appellant arguments, with no patient eligibility facts, visit records or hours furnished. Coverage is therefore not supported.
The facts are procedural only, with no clinical facts showing the IRF criteria were met. Coverage is therefore not supported.

Severe pain and IV/IM medication leave the beneficiary's ability to participate in intensive therapy unsettled, and the required plan of care and physician evaluation are not shown. Coverage is therefore not supported.
